name: Cuc Phuong: the Thousand-Year-Old Tree and Palace Cave
region: Cuc Phuong National Park, Ninh Binh
why: A loop through Vietnam's oldest national park: limestone forest, a cave climbed by steep steps and a giant tree with buttress roots taller than a person.
book: Buy the park permit at the headquarters, about 40 km from Ninh Binh (1-2 hours by car or motorbike taxi), then drive on to the park centre at Bong, where the loop starts. Guides can be hired at the park.
water: Carry 1.5 litres; drinks and food at the canteen in Bong.
dangers: Slippery limestone and roots after rain; steep stone steps to the cave.
Leeches in the wet season: long trousers and socks over them.
Hot and humid from May to September, with heavy rain.
turnaround: Not at the tree 2 hours after leaving Bong, or in heavy rain: go back the way you came.

points.name: Bong park centre, Cuc Phuong forest
points.note: Guest house, canteen and the information desk in a clearing of the primary forest. The marked trail leaves north into the trees.

points.name: Palace Cave (Động Sơn Cung)
points.note: A short, steep flight of steps leads up to the cave mouth. Bring a torch to look inside.

points.name: Thousand-Year-Old Tree (Cây Chò Ngàn Năm)
points.note: A giant forest tree with huge buttress roots, partly dying of age. The loop returns south to the end of the park road and back to Bong.
